question: What are the three main parts of the epidemiological triangle?
explanation: You nailed it! The epidemiological triangle consists of the infectious agent, the host who can catch it, and the environment where they meet.

question: How does keeping a community clean and sanitary help stop the spread of disease using the epidemiological triangle?

options.A: It alters the environment to prevent agent-host contact
options.B: It permanently alters the immune system of the host
options.C: It transforms a viral agent into a harmless bacterium
options.D: It directly destroys the genetic material of the agent

explanation: Great thinking! Good sanitation changes the environment so germs have a much harder time traveling from their source to a human host.

question: What do we call the natural home where germs live, grow, and multiply?
explanation: Spot on! A reservoir can be a human, animal, plant, or soil where germs hang out and multiply.

question: A nurse puts on gloves before emptying a patient's urine bag. Which part of the chain of infection is the nurse blocking?
explanation: You got it! Gloves act as a physical barrier, stopping the germs from hitching a ride onto the nurse's hands.

question: Which type of infection control precautions must you practice with every single patient you care for?
explanation: Awesome! Standard precautions are our everyday baseline protection for every patient, no matter their diagnosis.

question: A patient arrives with active pulmonary tuberculosis (TB). What kind of precautions should you set up right away?
explanation: Correct! TB travels easily through tiny air particles, so you need airborne precautions like a special room and an N95 mask.

question: What is the main difference between medical asepsis (clean technique) and surgical asepsis (sterile technique)?

options.A: Surgical asepsis relies entirely on chemical disinfectants rather than physical barriers
options.B: Surgical asepsis eliminates all microorganisms, while medical asepsis reduces their number and spread
options.C: Medical asepsis is used only in operating theatres, while surgical asepsis is for general wards
options.D: Medical asepsis destroys bacterial spores, whereas surgical asepsis only targets viruses

explanation: Well done! Clean technique (medical asepsis) cuts down germ numbers, while sterile technique (surgical asepsis) wipes out every single micro-organism.

question: Which process is required to make surgical tools safe if they will enter sterile body tissues?
explanation: You're doing great! Tools going inside sterile tissues must undergo sterilization to destroy all microscopic life and spores.

question: What kind of immunity does a baby get when receiving antibodies through breast milk?
explanation: Spot on! Because the baby receives ready-made antibodies naturally from the mother, it's natural passive immunity.

question: Why is herd immunity so helpful for vulnerable people in a community?

options.A: It guarantees that every single person in the population will develop permanent natural immunity
options.B: It completely eliminates all known environmental reservoirs of a bacterial pathogen
options.C: It transforms live vaccines into safer, non-replicating subunit vaccines
options.D: It reduces overall disease spread, indirectly protecting those who cannot be vaccinated

explanation: Brilliant! When most people are vaccinated, germs struggle to spread, keeping even the unvaccinated safe.

question: What is the biggest cause of antimicrobial resistance today?

options.A: Misuse and overuse of antimicrobial drugs
options.D: Strict adherence to sterile surgical techniques

explanation: Exactly right! Taking antibiotics when we don't need them—or not finishing the full dose—teaches germs how to survive our drugs.

question: A patient asks you for antibiotics to treat a mild cold (a virus). How should you reply?

options.A: Advise the patient to take a double dose to clear the viral symptoms faster
options.B: Encourage the patient to find a different clinic that will prescribe the medication
options.C: Suggest saving leftover antibiotics from a previous prescription for this illness
options.D: Explain that antibiotics only treat bacterial infections and will not cure a virus

explanation: Wonderful nursing response! Patient education stops drug resistance in its tracks.

question: What is the main difference between isolation and quarantine?

options.A: Isolation separates infected individuals, while quarantine separates exposed individuals
options.B: Quarantine applies only to bacterial infections, while isolation applies to viruses
options.C: Quarantine is used exclusively in hospitals, while isolation is used only at home
options.D: Isolation restricts healthy people, whereas quarantine treats sick patients

explanation: You've got it! Isolation is for people who are already sick, while quarantine is for people who were exposed and might get sick.

question: Why do we put healthy-feeling people into quarantine after a known exposure to a contagious illness?

options.A: To monitor them through the incubation period before they can spread the disease asymptomatically
options.B: To punish individuals who failed to maintain proper personal hygiene standards
options.C: To immediately administer therapeutic antibiotics regardless of the actual pathogen involved
options.D: To provide them with active immunity through immediate vaccination in a controlled facility

explanation: Spot on! It catches sneaky infections early so they don't pass them on to others before showing symptoms.

question: What is the main goal of public health surveillance for infectious diseases?

options.A: Ongoing collection and analysis of health data to guide public health action
options.B: Enforcing strict legal penalties for healthcare facilities that break sterile technique
options.C: Manufacture of safe and effective vaccines for global distribution
options.D: Providing emergency medical treatment to individual hospital patients

explanation: Correct! Tracking disease numbers helps public health teams spot trends and stop outbreaks early.

question: You notice three patients on your ward develop the same severe stomach bug within 24 hours. What should you do first?

options.A: Report the cluster to infection control and public health authorities
options.B: Prescribe broad-spectrum antibiotics to all patients on the ward
options.C: Discharge all unaffected patients immediately to clear the ward
options.D: Wait another week to see if more patients develop the same symptoms

explanation: Great clinical judgment! Quick reporting helps infection control teams step in and stop an outbreak before it grows.
